Hadhrat Amr bin Dinaar narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) made up his mind not to marry, (his sister) Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) said to him, "Get married because if your children pass away, you will be rewarded (for your patience) and if they live, they will make du'aa for you."[^2]
The Words of Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) on the Way to the Battle of Siffeen

Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abza (RA) reports that en route to Siffeen when he was on the bank of the Euphrates River, Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) said, "O Allaah! If I knew that you would be pleased with me for throwing myself off a mountain and rolling down as I fall, I would certainly do so. O Allaah! If I knew that you would be pleased with me for kindling a large fire and throwing myself into it, I would certainly do so. O Allaah! If I knew that you would be pleased with me for throwing myself into the water and drowning, I would certainly do so. O Allaah! I am fighting only to please You and I am certain that you will never make me unsuccessful as long as I do things to please You."[^3]
The Statement of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) Concerning his Actions after the Demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas (RA)
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas (RA) once said, "For me to do a good deed today is more beloved to me than two liked deeds done during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ because when we were with Rasulullaah ﷺ, our only concern was the Aakhirah and not this world. Today, however, the world has fallen for us."[^4]
The Exertion of Our Guide Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Alqama narrates that he once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "was Rasulullaah ﷺ in the habit of specially setting aside certain days (for worship)?" "Not at all," Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) replied, "His deeds were perpetual, but which any of you is capable of doing what Rasulullaah ﷺ did?"[^5]
